beats.text: A log grows forever. You want the latest value per key.
beats.say: A log keeps growing forever. But often you only care about the latest value for each key, like a user's current email address.

beats.text: Retention deletes by age: a key can vanish.
beats.say: Normal retention deletes old data by age or size, even when it is the only record for a key. That erases the key completely.

beats.text: Compaction keeps the latest value per key.
beats.say: Log compaction works differently. It keeps at least the latest value for every key, and removes the older values of the same key.
To delete a key, you write a tombstone, a message with a null value. After a while, compaction removes the key entirely.

beats.text: A compacted topic is a table you can rebuild.
beats.say: A compacted topic behaves like a table. A new consumer reads it from the start, and rebuilds the current state. Kafka does this for its own consumer offsets.

beats.text: Offsets have gaps. It runs in the background.
beats.say: Offsets never change, so the log has gaps. And compaction runs in the background, so you may briefly still see old values.

beats.text: That wraps up the stream series!
beats.say: That wraps up the stream series. Follow for more system design.
